title: Modern History: Extremist Movements (Past Year Questions)

questions.q_en:
Under the leadership of which of the following revolutionaries was the Chittagong Armoury Raid conducted?

Options:
questions.solution_en:
· The Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930) was a revolutionary uprising against British rule in India.

· It was planned and led by Surya Sen, popularly known as Masterda.

· Rash Behari Bose and Badal Gupta were associated with other revolutionary activities, and Hemu Kalani was a revolutionary from Sindh.
questions.solution_hi:
• चटगाँव शस्त्रागार छापा (1930) भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन के विरुद्ध एक क्रांतिकारी विद्रोह था।

• इसकी योजना व नेतृत्व सूर्य सेन, जिन्हें आमतौर पर मास्टरदा कहा जाता है, ने किया था।

• रास बिहारी बोस व बादल गुप्ता अन्य क्रांतिकारी गतिविधियों से जुड़े थे, व हेमू कलानी सिंध से एक क्रांतिकारी थे।

questions.q_en: Who among the following assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London?
questions.solution_en: Wyllie worked with charities and associations related to India. At a reception given by one such association - the National Indian Association - in 1909, Wyllie was shot by Madan Lal Dhingra, an Indian student. A Parsee physician, Dr Cawas Lalcaca, who sought to protect Wyllie, was also killed. Dhingra and his family were known to Wyllie from his time in India, and Dhingra's family had maintained a correspondence with Wyllie. Dhingra had himself ignored letters from Wyllie suggesting a meeting at India House. Some argue that Dhingra's preferred target was either the former Secretary of State Lord Morley or the former Viceroy Lord Curzon, given their greater prestige and connection with the construction of repressive policies against revolutionaries in India; Dhingra was known to have been following both men. Wyllie's presence at events with Indian students, however, made him an easier target.
questions.solution_hi: वायली भारत से संबंधित दान संस्थाओं व संघों के साथ कार्य करते थे। 1909 में एक ऐसे संघ - नेशनल इंडियन एसोसिएशन - द्वारा दिए गए स्वागत समारोह में, वायली को एक भारतीय छात्र मदन लाल ढींगरा ने गोली मार दी। वायली की रक्षा का प्रयास करने वाले एक पारसी चिकित्सक, डॉ. कावस लालकाका की भी मृत्यु हो गई।

questions.q_en: Moplahs, or Muslim peasants, created a powerful anti-zamindar movement in:
questions.solution_en: The Moplah Rebellion, also known as the Malabar Rebellion, took place in the Malabar region of Kerala during 1921. The Moplahs, who were predominantly Muslim peasants, led this movement against the oppressive policies of the landlords or zamindars and the British colonial administration.
questions.solution_hi: मोपला विद्रोह, जिसे मालाबार विद्रोह भी कहा जाता है, 1921 में केरल के मालाबार क्षेत्र में हुआ। मोपला, जो मुख्यतः मुस्लिम किसान थे, ने जमींदारों की दमनकारी नीतियों व ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक प्रशासन के विरुद्ध इस आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किया।

questions.q_en: At which of the following jails was Khudiram Bose sent to the gallows?
questions.solution_en:
Khudiram Bose was the youngest revolutionary freedom fighter who was executed on August 11, 1908 for his role in the Muzaffarpur conspiracy case. Khudiram Bose, along with another freedom fighter Prafulla Chaki, tried to assassinate a British judge, Douglas Kingsford. The bombs did not hit the judge's carriage but hit a different one, leading to the death of two others.

Prafulla Chaki committed suicide before the police could arrest him. Khudiram Bose was arrested and later he was sentenced to death. He was only 18, when he was hanged at the Muzaffarpur Jail, which has been renamed after him.
questions.solution_hi: खुदीराम बोस सबसे युवा क्रांतिकारी स्वतंत्रता सेनानी थे जिन्हें मुजफ्फरपुर षड्यंत्र मामले में उनकी भूमिका हेतु 11 अगस्त 1908 को फाँसी दी गई। खुदीराम बोस ने, एक अन्य स्वतंत्रता सेनानी प्रफुल्ल चाकी के साथ, ब्रिटिश न्यायाधीश डगलस किंग्सफोर्ड की हत्या का प्रयास किया। बम न्यायाधीश की गाड़ी पर नहीं बल्कि एक अलग गाड़ी पर गिरा।

questions.q_en: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote the novel Anand Math based on which of the following rebellions/revolts?
questions.solution_en:
• Anand Math, written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, is set against the backdrop of the Sanyasi Rebellion (late 18th century).

• The novel inspired Indian nationalism and contains the famous song "Vande Mataram".

• The Sanyasi Rebellion involved Hindu ascetics (sanyasis) who fought against British colonial rule in Bengal.
questions.solution_hi:
• बंकिम चंद्र चट्टोपाध्याय द्वारा लिखित आनंद मठ, संन्यासी विद्रोह (18वीं सदी के अंत) की पृष्ठभूमि पर आधारित है।

• इस उपन्यास ने भारतीय राष्ट्रवाद को प्रेरित किया और इसमें प्रसिद्ध गीत "वंदे मातरम्" शामिल है।

• संन्यासी विद्रोह में हिंदू संन्यासी शामिल थे जिन्होंने संघर्ष किया।

questions.q_en: In which of the following areas did the Uprising of Khurda in 1817 take place?
questions.solution_en: The Paika Rebellion or Uprising of Khurda took place in 1817 in Khurda, Odisha. It was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu against the British East India Company and is considered one of the first armed rebellions against British rule in India.
questions.solution_hi: पाइका विद्रोह या खुर्दा का विद्रोह 1817 में ओडिशा के खुर्दा में हुआ था। इसका नेतृत्व बख्शी जगबंधु ने ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के विरुद्ध किया और इसे भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन के विरुद्ध पहले सशस्त्र विद्रोहों में से एक माना जाता है।

questions.q_en: Which revolutionary organisation was established at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi in 1928?
questions.solution_en:
· The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, New Delhi, by revolutionaries including Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and others.

· It emerged from the earlier Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) and aimed to overthrow British rule through armed struggle, inspired by socialist ideals.

· The HSRA is renowned for the Kakori Conspiracy (1925), Saunders' assassination (1928), and the Lahore Conspiracy Case (1931).

Why not the others?

· Indian Home Rule Society: Founded by Shyamji Krishna Varma in London (1905) to promote self-rule, unrelated to HSRA.

· Bharat Naujawan Sabha: Established by Bhagat Singh in Punjab (1926) as a youth organization.

· Swadesh Bandhab Samiti: A Bengal-based revolutionary group (early 1900s) led by Ashwini Kumar Dutta, focused on swadeshi and boycott movements.
questions.solution_hi:
• हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HSRA) की स्थापना 1928 में नई दिल्ली के फिरोज शाह कोटला में हुई थी, जिसमें चंद्रशेखर आजाद, भगत सिंह, सुखदेव व अन्य क्रांतिकारी शामिल थे।

• यह पहले की हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HRA) से उभरा और सशस्त्र क्रांति के माध्यम से ब्रिटिश शासन को उखाड़ फेंकने का लक्ष्य रखता था।

questions.q_en: What was the age in years of the revolutionary Bhagat Singh when he was hanged till death?
questions.solution_en: The revolutionary freedom fighter Bhagat Singh was hanged till death at the age of 23.
questions.solution_hi: क्रांतिकारी स्वतंत्रता सेनानी भगत सिंह को 23 वर्ष की आयु में फाँसी दी गई थी।

questions.q_en: Who among the following was primarily an integral part of the Indian National Army (INA)?
questions.solution_en:
· Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army (INA), which was formed in 1942 during World War II.

· The INA fought against British colonial rule in India with support from Japan and Germany.

· His famous slogan "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom" inspired Indians to join the struggle.

· The Azad Hind Fauj (another name for INA) played a significant role in India's independence movement.

· Unlike Gandhi's non-violent approach, Bose believed in armed struggle to achieve freedom.

Incorrect Options:

· Rabindranath Tagore was a poet and philosopher, not a military leader.

· Chittaranjan Das was a politician and lawyer, associated with the Swaraj Party.

· Abanindranath Tagore was an artist and founder of the Bengal School of Art.
questions.solution_hi:
• सुभाष चंद्र बोस ने भारतीय राष्ट्रीय सेना (INA) का नेतृत्व किया, जिसका गठन द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान 1942 में हुआ था।

• INA ने जापान व जर्मनी के समर्थन से भारत में ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के विरुद्ध युद्ध लड़ा।

• उनके प्रसिद्ध नारे "तुम मुझे खून दो, मैं तुम्हें आजादी दूँगा" ने भारतीयों को संघर्ष में शामिल होने हेतु प्रेरित किया।

questions.q_en: Sido and Kanhu were leaders of which of the following tribal rebellions?
questions.solution_en:
· Sido and Kanhu Murmu led the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) against the British East India Company and oppressive landlords (zamindars) in present-day Jharkhand, Bihar, and West Bengal.

· The rebellion was caused by exploitative revenue policies, forced labor, and high-interest loans by moneylenders.

Other rebellions:

· Moplah Rebellion (1921) - A peasant uprising in Kerala against British rule and landlords.

· Kol Rebellion (1831-32) - A tribal revolt in Chotanagpur against British rule.

· Munda Rebellion (1899-1900) - Led by Birsa Munda, it was against British policies that disrupted tribal customs.
questions.solution_hi:
• सिदो व कान्हू मुर्मू ने वर्तमान झारखंड, बिहार व पश्चिम बंगाल में ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी व दमनकारी जमींदारों के विरुद्ध संथाल विद्रोह (1855-56) का नेतृत्व किया।

• यह विद्रोह शोषणकारी राजस्व नीतियों, जबरन श्रम व साहूकारों द्वारा उच्च ब्याज ऋणों के कारण हुआ था।

questions.q_en: Which of the following revolutionaries was arrested by the British as an accused in the Alipore Bomb Conspiracy Case?
questions.solution_en: Kanailal Dutta was a revolutionary who was arrested by the British as an accused in the Alipore Bomb Conspiracy Case.
questions.solution_hi: कनाईलाल दत्त एक क्रांतिकारी थे जिन्हें अलीपुर बम षड्यंत्र मामले में अभियुक्त के रूप में अंग्रेजों द्वारा गिरफ्तार किया गया था।

questions.q_en: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in______.
questions.solution_en: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded in 1928. The HSRA, also known as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army, was a revolutionary party set up by Chandrasekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and others in Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi.
questions.solution_hi: हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HSRA) की स्थापना 1928 में हुई। HSRA, जिसे हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन आर्मी भी कहा जाता है, एक क्रांतिकारी दल था जिसे चंद्रशेखर आजाद, भगत सिंह, सुखदेव व अन्य ने नई दिल्ली के फिरोज शाह कोटला में स्थापित किया था।

questions.q_en: "Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas" is observed on the birth anniversary of________.
questions.solution_en: "Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas" is observed on the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda. Birsa Munda was a tribal freedom fighter, religious leader, and folk hero who played a significant role in the tribal rights movement against the British colonial rule in India.
questions.solution_hi: "जनजातीय गौरव दिवस" बिरसा मुंडा की जयंती पर मनाया जाता है। बिरसा मुंडा एक आदिवासी स्वतंत्रता सेनानी, धार्मिक नेता व लोक नायक थे जिन्होंने भारत में ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के विरुद्ध आदिवासी अधिकार आंदोलन में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई।

questions.q_en: Which of the following revolutionary groups' members assassinated Assistant Superintendent of Police John Saunders in 1927?
questions.solution_en: In December 1928, Bhagat Singh and Shivaram Rajguru, members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) previously known as the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), shot and killed British police officer John Saunders in Lahore, Punjab.
questions.solution_hi: दिसंबर 1928 में, हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HSRA), जिसे पहले हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HRA) कहा जाता था, के सदस्यों भगत सिंह व शिवराम राजगुरु ने लाहौर, पंजाब में ब्रिटिश पुलिस अधिकारी जॉन सॉन्डर्स को गोली मारकर हत्या कर दी।

questions.q_en: The Ghadar Party was founded in _______ by Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kanshi Ram, Harnam Singh Tundilat, Lala Har Dayal, and others.
questions.solution_en: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco, USA, by Sohan Singh Bhakna, Lala Har Dayal, Kanshi Ram, and other Indian revolutionaries. Its aim was to overthrow British rule in India through an armed revolution. The party played a crucial role in spreading nationalist ideas among Indian immigrants, especially in the United States and Canada.
questions.solution_hi: गदर पार्टी की स्थापना 1913 में अमेरिका के सैन फ्रांसिस्को में सोहन सिंह भकना, लाला हरदयाल, कांशी राम व अन्य भारतीय क्रांतिकारियों ने की थी। इसका उद्देश्य सशस्त्र क्रांति के माध्यम से भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन को उखाड़ फेंकना था।

questions.q_en: Who among the following was the founder of 'Tiger Legion' or 'Free India Legion'?
questions.solution_en: Subhas Chandra Bose started the 'Tiger Legion' or 'Free India Legion', a military unit to fight the British in the Second World War. He got support from the German government and army. He gave them the slogan 'Jai Hind' and the tiger emblem.
questions.solution_hi: सुभाष चंद्र बोस ने द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध में अंग्रेजों से लड़ने हेतु 'टाइगर लीजन' या 'फ्री इंडिया लीजन' नामक एक सैन्य इकाई शुरू की। उन्हें जर्मन सरकार व सेना से समर्थन मिला। उन्होंने उन्हें 'जय हिंद' का नारा व बाघ का प्रतीक दिया।

questions.q_en: The Indian National Army was formed in which of the following countries?
questions.solution_en: The Indian National Army (INA) was formed in Singapore in 1942 under the leadership of Subhas Chandra Bose. The INA aimed to secure Indian independence from British rule with Japanese support during World War II.
questions.solution_hi: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय सेना (INA) का गठन 1942 में सिंगापुर में सुभाष चंद्र बोस के नेतृत्व में हुआ था। INA का उद्देश्य द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के दौरान जापानी समर्थन से भारत को ब्रिटिश शासन से स्वतंत्रता दिलाना था।

questions.q_en: In order to overturn the British rule through arms, the Kakori Conspiracy was planned by the members of the _________ in 1925.
questions.solution_en: The Kakori Conspiracy, planned in 1925, was orchestrated by members of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), later renamed as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). It aimed to challenge British rule through armed resistance and targeted actions, such as the robbery of a train near Kakori to acquire funds for revolutionary activities.
questions.solution_hi: 1925 में योजनाबद्ध काकोरी षड्यंत्र, हिंदुस्तान रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HRA) के सदस्यों द्वारा रचा गया था, जिसे बाद में हिंदुस्तान सोशलिस्ट रिपब्लिकन एसोसिएशन (HSRA) नाम दिया गया। इसका उद्देश्य क्रांतिकारी गतिविधियों हेतु धन जुटाने के लिए काकोरी के पास एक ट्रेन लूट जैसी सशस्त्र प्रतिरोध कार्रवाइयों के माध्यम से ब्रिटिश शासन को चुनौती देना था।

questions.q_en: Who was martyred after a 63-day hunger strike during the Lahore conspiracy case trial?
questions.solution_en:
Jatindra Nath Das died after a 63-day hunger strike in jail, protesting against poor conditions for political prisoners.

· Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929 - 30): A trial following revolutionary activities against British rule, notably the bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.

· Hunger Strike Context: Political prisoners, including Bhagat Singh and Jatindra Nath Das, undertook a hunger strike in Lahore's Central Jail to protest inhumane conditions, demanding better treatment.

· Jatindra Nath Das: A revolutionary, Das continued the strike for 63 days, from June to September 1929, and died on September 13, 1929, due to starvation and medical neglect.

· Other Options:

o Ram Prasad Bismil: Executed in 1927 for the Kakori Conspiracy Case.

o Prafulla Chaki: Died by suicide in 1908 during the Muzaffarpur bombing.

o Rash Behari Bose: Fled to Japan, died in 1945, not involved in the Lahore case.
questions.solution_hi:
जतींद्र नाथ दास ने जेल में राजनीतिक कैदियों की खराब स्थितियों के विरुद्ध विरोध करते हुए 63 दिनों की भूख हड़ताल के बाद प्राण त्याग दिए।

• लाहौर षड्यंत्र मामला (1929-30): भगत सिंह व बटुकेश्वर दत्त द्वारा केंद्रीय विधान सभा में बम फेंकने सहित ब्रिटिश शासन के विरुद्ध क्रांतिकारी गतिविधियों के बाद हुआ मुकदमा।

questions.q_en: The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in which of the following present states of India?
questions.solution_en:
· The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in the present-day state of Maharashtra.

· The Ramoshis were a tribal community traditionally employed as watchmen and soldiers under the Maratha Empire.

· After the British took over, many Ramoshis were rendered unemployed, leading to discontent.

· The revolt was led by Chittur Singh, and later by Vasudev Balwant Phadke, who is also associated with mobilizing Ramoshis in later uprisings.

Further Insight:

· Tamil Nadu - Known for revolts like the Vellore Mutiny.

· West Bengal - Associated with revolts like the Santhal Rebellion and Indigo Revolt.
questions.solution_hi:
• 1824 का रामोशी विद्रोह वर्तमान महाराष्ट्र राज्य में हुआ था।

• रामोशी एक आदिवासी समुदाय था जो पारंपरिक रूप से मराठा साम्राज्य के अधीन चौकीदार व सैनिक के रूप में नियोजित था।

• अंग्रेजों के अधिग्रहण के बाद, कई रामोशी बेरोजगार हो गए, जिससे असंतोष उत्पन्न हुआ।
